claims.statement: `manage.sh` is an interactive control panel that delegates engine actions to `setup-qwen38-pi.sh`; the engine exposes explicit commands, while `status` is read-only and uses `/v1/models?autoload=0` rather than generating output or autoloading a model.

Both shell entry points source `lib/local-ai-common.sh`, whose helpers validate regular non-symlink API-key files and pass the bearer header to curl through stdin configuration so the token is not placed in curl argv.

Supported configuration resolves in explicit environment-variable, saved `setup.env`, then built-in-default order; the engine reads and writes only a fixed key set, validates values, and atomically writes a mode-0600 regular non-symlink `setup.env`.

`apply` reruns planning, snapshots desired-state, routing, launcher, preset, and unit files, then persists configuration, updates routing/agent launchers, and invokes the service; failures restore snapshots so routing failures do not change the router and router failures restore prior files.

The model lock is a pipe-delimited artifact contract with tier, variant, router ID, model directory, immutable revision, remote path, exact size, SHA-256, and kind; selected tiers include their `ALL` artifacts, and the concrete manifest defines everyday, coder, and senior artifacts and aliases.

Before generating a service, the engine requires at least one complete tier, verifies its locked artifacts, refuses incomplete selected everyday/startup tiers, and emits preset sections only for available tiers.

`MODELS_MAX` is validated as exactly 1 on the target; the generated launcher passes `--models-max` and `--models-autoload`; and only the available configured startup tier is marked `load-on-startup`, with `none` producing a cold router.

The generated launcher binds llama-server to `127.0.0.1`, reads an API-key file and a generated models preset; the generated user unit limits privileges and writes through systemd protections while granting read-only model access and DRM device access.

Service generation rejects custom, mixed, symlinked, or non-regular managed-trio paths; it stages and validates preset/launcher/unit files, backs up prior state, and rolls back files and systemd enabled/active state if activation or readiness fails.

The service creates or validates a regular 0600 local API key, and readiness requires an unauthenticated protected request to be rejected, an authenticated request to be accepted, a matching authenticated router catalog, and—on Linux—proof that the managed MainPID owns the listener; a configured startup model must become loaded or sleeping.

Generated OMP configuration declares an authenticated loopback OpenAI-compatible provider for complete model tiers, disables OMP's implicit keyless llama.cpp provider, and limits both task concurrency and llama.cpp in-flight requests to one.

OMP routing selects the first complete tier in everyday/coder/senior order as base, promotes complete coder and senior tiers for specialist and architect roles, applies sticky/balanced/quality profile choices, and generates tier-forcing wrappers only for complete models.

OMP's `models.yml` and `config.yml` are handled as an atomic ownership pair: custom files are preserved with example candidates unless forced, and routing updates snapshot and restore the pair and wrappers on failure or interruption.

The generated selected-agent wrapper verifies and exports the local key and loopback URLs for the selected `omp` or `pi` binary without overwriting an unmarked user-owned launcher; normal agent installation leaves an existing binary untouched, and `agent-upgrade` is the explicit replacement path.

`status` probes loopback independently of systemd state and reports authenticated, insecure, unauthorized, down, or error from unauthenticated and authenticated protected/catalog probes; `smoke` confirms the auth wall and then sends a tier-specific authenticated chat request.

`install.sh` delegates installation to the engine's `all` command, and `all` checks the workstation, persists configuration after checking, installs prerequisites, requires a reboot before model/GPU work when needed, then provisions the Everyday model, service, selected agent, and desktop integration.

The installed `local-ai` front door sends menu and logs requests to the interactive manager or user-service journal, forwards other commands to the engine, and uses Omarchy's terminal helper or `xdg-terminal-exec` for desktop invocations.
Desktop integration creates only marked user launchers and XDG desktop entries, preserves unmarked or symlinked paths, and removes only entries it recognizes as managed.
On Omarchy, the agent library isolates the project's pinned `pi` and `omp` binaries in a private local-AI prefix and does not treat Omarchy's moving launcher stubs as installed project agents.

Mutating lifecycle commands acquire one private per-user operation lock independent of the configurable model directory, preventing concurrent work from racing shared configuration, agent routing, service, and system resources.

Platform package installation requires an Omarchy Linux target, rejects pending system upgrades, verifies packages in configured repositories before sudo, and does not add repositories or fall back to unreviewed source/AUR installation.
